name: Rowan Davis
life: “I still remember reading shop notices with the help of the lunchtime cleaner.” Thursday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Rowan notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I took the day off with a stomach ache. I don't want my boss at the bank to know I'm learning to read his notices.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a boxy denim jacket and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. Rowan has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Rowan rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket during a conversation.
personality: Rowan finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To read workplace notices without disclosing the class.
family: Fiona Mann is Rowan’s half-sibling. Rowan is free to hang up first. Fiona makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The bitter orange*, Fiona says, “I can't eat the memorial sandwich. I chose the paper it will be wrapped in.”
connections: Yvette Tsai. Two workers using different strategies for private reading try the same examination paper.

reactions.situation: An examiner offers to read a question aloud
reactions.response: Rowan asks the learner how they want the question presented before the examiner begins.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Rowan says what they know in their own name and refuses to treat a guess as something the child has to disprove.

reactions.situation: When thanked for a shared success
reactions.response: Rowan points to the person who noticed the original mistake.
